findings.description: State variables (migrationInfo, yieldStrategy) written after external call to strategy.withdraw via _routeExit. Function is nonReentrant; strategy is owner-set/trusted. Cross-function reentrancy only reachable through pendingReward (view). Residual risk only if the owner-configured yield strategy is malicious/compromised.

findings.description: pool.totalStaked / user.amount / user.rewardDebt written after external calls phUSD.mint (in _settle) and strategy.deposit (in _routeDeposit). Function is nonReentrant; phUSD and strategy are trusted/owner-set. CEI deviation, defense-in-depth only.

Same CEI deviation pattern as stake: pool.totalStaked / info.amount / info.rewardDebt written after phUSD.mint and strategy.deposit. Function is nonReentrant and onlyMigrator (trusted caller). Defense-in-depth only.

Return value of EnumerableSet.add/remove (and strategy.deposit at L215) ignored at lines 215, 254, 274, 314, 477, 535. add/remove are idempotent so ignoring the bool is benign by design; the ignored strategy.deposit return at setYieldStrategy (idle-balance sweep) is the only one worth a glance. QA at most.

External call (phUSD.mint via _settle inside _exitPosition) executed inside the per-user loop of batchMigrate; mirrored in StableStakerMigrator.migrate (depositFor in loop, L61). Gas/DoS consideration for large batches — caller controls batch size off-chain via getStakersRange, so QA/operational note.
